title: Extrema & the Mean Value Theorem
summary: Maxima and minima occur at critical points (where $f'=0$ or is undefined) or endpoints. The Extreme Value Theorem guarantees them on a closed interval, and the Mean Value Theorem guarantees a point where the instantaneous rate equals the average rate.

critical point.in_class: The only interior candidates for a max or min.

absolute extremum.plain: The overall highest or lowest value on an interval.
absolute extremum.in_class: Found among critical points and endpoints.

local extremum.plain: A peak or valley relative to nearby points.
local extremum.in_class: Occurs at a critical point where $f'$ changes sign.

Extreme Value Theorem.plain: A continuous function on $[a,b]$ attains a max and a min.
Extreme Value Theorem.in_class: Guarantees extrema exist to search for.

closed interval method.plain: Compare $f$ at all critical points and both endpoints.
closed interval method.in_class: The largest is the max, the smallest the min.

Rolle's Theorem.plain: Equal endpoints ⇒ a flat spot in between.

Mean Value Theorem.plain: Some instant matches the average rate.

average rate.in_class: $\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$; the MVT says a tangent matches it.

concept_sections.heading: Critical points
concept_sections.explanation: Interior extrema can only happen where the slope is zero or undefined — the critical points. Find them by solving $f'(x)=0$ and noting where $f'$ fails to exist.
math_steps: Add any $x$ where $f'$ is undefined (but $f$ is defined).

concept_sections.heading: Absolute extrema on $[a,b]$
concept_sections.explanation: By the Extreme Value Theorem a continuous function on a closed interval has an absolute max and min. Evaluate $f$ at every critical point and both endpoints and compare.
math_steps: List critical points in $[a,b]$ and the endpoints.

concept_sections.heading: Classifying with the first derivative
concept_sections.explanation: At a critical point, if $f'$ switches $+\to-$ it's a local max; $-\to+$ a local min; no sign change means neither.
math_steps: Test the sign of $f'$ on each side.

concept_sections.heading: Rolle's Theorem
concept_sections.explanation: If $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$, differentiable inside, and $f(a)=f(b)$, then somewhere the tangent is horizontal: $f'(c)=0$.

concept_sections.heading: The Mean Value Theorem
concept_sections.explanation: Under the same smoothness, some interior point's slope equals the average slope: $f'(c)=\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$. It links average and instantaneous rates.

real_world_examples.title: Maximum height of a projectile
real_world_examples.scenario: A ball's height peaks then falls.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The maximum is a critical point where velocity (the derivative) is zero.

real_world_examples.title: Speed-camera average
real_world_examples.scenario: Two cameras time a car over a stretch.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The MVT guarantees the car actually hit its average speed at some instant — the basis of average-speed enforcement.

real_world_examples.title: Best and worst of a season
real_world_examples.scenario: A stock's price over a fixed window.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Absolute extrema on the interval identify the peak and trough values.
